Rule: A.1 item 114 'Line delimiter, specification of. This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (9.1.13.2 ... I-O Status = 06, 12.4.5.10, ORGANIZATION clause, General rule 2)' (cite.py --check A.1 "Line delimiter, specification of" -> OK §A.1 114)). Operative text §12.4.5.10.3 GR2: 'Each record in a line sequential file is terminated by an implementor-defined line delimiter' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 -> OK §12.4.5.10.3 2); NB the Annex's '12.4.5.10' alone FAILS --check, the rule sits in the General rules subclause .3). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-114 |' row. The only mention is off-key inside DOC-A.1-115 (the character-set row): 'the two line delimiters CR U+000D and LF U+000A' - which names the characters excluded from the set but does not state the delimiter a WRITE emits nor the READ-side recognition rule. Code fixes both halves: OpenWriter builds the write handle with NewLine = "
" (every WRITE ends the record with CR LF); ReadPhysicalLine accepts LF, lone CR, or CR LF as the terminator, and a final line with no terminator ends at EOF. Probes: ls1.cob (--std 2023) writes 'AB' and 'CDE' -> od shows 'A B  
 C D E  
'; ls2.cob reading 'AAAAAAAABB
CC' with PIC X(5) -> [AAAAA] 06, [AAA  ] 00, [BB   ] 00, [CC   ] 00, then 10 - so lone CR, lone LF and EOF all delimit and the §9.1.13.2 '06' arm fires on the over-length line. The behaviour is settled and plausible, but the required documentation under its own key is absent -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Editions: ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL is a 2023 introduction (per DOC-A.1-115's own ONE EDITION paragraph). No spec-derived test pins the delimiter bytes. Owning note: none item-specific (grep 'item 114' / 'DOC-A.1-114' / 'line delimiter' in kb/Work: only unrelated hits); umbrella kb/Work A11 and the register campaign kb/Work PB160.

Rule: A.1 item 116 'Linkage section (whether access to linkage section items is meaningful when called from a non-COBOL program). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for calling a COBOL program from a non-COBOL program. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented... (13.7, Linkage section)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 116)). Operative text §13.7.4 GR3: 'If a program is activated by a non-COBOL runtime element, the implementor defines whether access to formal parameters and the returning item is guaranteed' (cite.py --check 13.7.4 "the implementor defines whether access to formal parameters and the returning item is guaranteed" -> OK §13.7.4 3)); GR5's non-COBOL-activator sentence (initial value of linkage items) is its twin. The CONDITION HOLDS: CONFORMANCE.md §3's 'Return to a NON-COBOL activating runtime element' bullet (kb/Work PB408) declares a .NET host activating a generated program to be a supported non-COBOL activator, and the public entry ProgramRegistry.CallProgram(name, callerPath, CobolArg[] args, CobolArg? returning, ...) maps a host's CobolArg[] positionally onto the LINKAGE formals exactly as ICobolProgram.Call does for a COBOL caller, while ICobolProgram.Activate leaves linkage UNBOUND (ProgramEmitter's UNBOUND seed, §13.7.4 GR3). So a determination exists in code (access guaranteed when the host passes args through CallProgram; unbound under Activate) but CONFORMANCE.md has NO '| DOC-A.1-116 |' row and the §3 bullet says nothing about linkage access -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Not re-reported: owning note kb/Work PB1253 (open, 'linkage-section' finding: 'Write DOC-A.1-116 ... item 116 also needs the behaviour DECIDED for ICobolProgram.Call/Activate entered without a COBOL caller'). Umbrella kb/Work A11. No spec-derived test drives a non-COBOL activator. Editions: LINKAGE SECTION and the non-COBOL-activator rule exist in every edition; the host ABI is edition-independent.

Rule: A.1 item 117 'Listings (whether and when produced by the compiler, effect of logical conversion). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (6.5, Logical conversion; Clause 7...; 7.3.18, LISTING directive, General rule 1)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 117)). §7.3.18.3 GR1 'Whether the compiler produces a source listing is implementor-defined. If the compiler does not produce a source listing, the LISTING directive shall be ignored.' (cite.py --check 7.3.18.3 -> OK §7.3.18.3 1); NB the Annex's '7.3.18 ... General rule 1' lives in subclause .3). §6.5 'The implementor shall define the effect on the source listing, if any, of logical conversion.' (cite.py --check 6.5 -> OK §6.5 9)). Code: COBOL.NET produces NO source listing - the CLI (cobol --help) has no listing option and no listing writer exists in src; >>LISTING is recognized and held as NONE HELD in DirectiveStateRegistry citing §7.3.18.3 GR1; probe lst.cob (>>LISTING OFF / >>PAGE / >>LISTING ON, --std 2023) compiles clean and prints HI. So 'whether' = never, 'when' = never, and the logical-conversion effect is vacuous - a coherent determination. CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-117 |' row; the no-listing fact appears only off-key in §3's recognized-and-inert directive prose ('>>LISTING / >>PAGE (§7.3.18 / §7.3.19) - no source listing is produced'), which the register/audit_annex_a1.py cannot see and which does not state the §6.5 half -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Not re-reported: owning note kb/Work PB1496 (open; 'write DOC-A.1-156, DOC-A.1-157 and DOC-A.1-117 rows'); also named in kb/Work PB1369 (open) and PB1067. Umbrella A11. Editions: 'whether a listing is produced' applies to every edition; the LISTING directive itself is 2002+ (ConstructRegistry listing-directive-2002).

Rule: A.1 item 118 'Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. The implementor may specify that the user locale and the system locale are the same locale. (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 118)). §8.2.1: 'The implementor shall specify the manner in which the user default locale is defined and shall provide at least one user default locale for use in computing environments that do not provide a user default locale' and the SYSTEM twin (both cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). No documentation obligation, so part (a) is waived (there is no '| DOC-A.1-118 |' row; the manner IS nevertheless written voluntarily: CONFORMANCE.md §4 A.4.9 locale paragraph 'the user default from COBOL_USER_LOCALE (else the process culture, else the root)', RuntimeConfig.All's COBOL_USER_LOCALE / COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE entries, DESIGN-locale-facility §4.3 table, DETERMINATION L2 = owner decision Q2). Part (b), the behaviour: LocaleState() sets UserDefault = Determine(COBOL_USER_LOCALE, CultureInfo.CurrentCulture) and SystemDefault = Determine(COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE, CultureInfo.InstalledUICulture); Determine returns the env value, else the culture name, else '' (the root) when the host has no culture data - so at least one user and one system default ALWAYS exist, including environments that supply none. SystemDefault has no setter (§8.2.1 'The capability of setting the system default locale from COBOL is not provided'). Probe loc.cob (--std 2023; SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT then FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE): env COBOL_USER_LOCALE=de-DE COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE=fr-FR -> SYS 24/09/2026, USR 24.09.2026 (two distinct defaults, each honoured); env unset + DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 -> both 09/24/2026, no exception, rc 0 (the root fallback). Tests: the unit test SetFromSystemDefault asserts CurrentLocale == SystemDefault; pb64t1_set_locale_categories runs SYSDEF/USERDEF arms under the harness's pinned INVARIANT defaults. Caveat for the refuter: no test pins the unset-env culture fallback arm (it is host-dependent by design); verified by probe only. Editions: the locale facility (A.4.9) is 2002+. Owning note: none (grep item 118: none); design owner kb/Work PB64 (landed T1).

Rule: A.1 item 119 'Locale specification (manner of implementation). This item is required because at least one default locale is required. This item does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 119)). §8.2.1: 'The format and implementation of locales may differ from those specifications provided that logically-equivalent functionality is supported.' and 'If the operating environment does not supply a default locale, it is implementor-defined.' (both cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). No documentation obligation, so part (a) is waived (no '| DOC-A.1-119 |' row; the manner is nevertheless described voluntarily in CONFORMANCE.md §4's A.4.9 locale paragraph and docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-locale-facility.md). Part (b): a locale IS implemented and a default always exists - locales are identified by BCP 47/CLDR tags normalized by LocaleIdentification (availability = CollationEngine.IsKnownLocale), with per-category state in LocaleState (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME), collation from COBOL.NET's own derived CLDR 48 / UCA 17 tables and the LC_MONETARY/LC_NUMERIC/LC_TIME facts read once per locale by LocaleFacts from the nearest predefined .NET culture; the root locale ('') is the implementor-supplied default when the environment supplies none (LocaleState.Determine). A.4.9 is CLAIMED WHOLE in CONFORMANCE.md §4. Probe loc.cob: SET LOCALE to SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT + LOCALE-DATE works with env-named defaults (fr-FR / de-DE formats differ) and with invariant globalization and no env (root, rc 0). Editions: 2002+ (the locale facility). Owning note: none (grep item 119: none); design owner kb/Work PB64.
